input.quote: 10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 10.3 is captioned "Assignment" but is only a binding-effect/successors-and-assigns clause: it neither confirms our right to assign to an affiliate or successor nor restricts HDI, so HDI is free to transfer this Agreement (potentially to a leather-goods competitor) without our consent. No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists anywhere (the only termination triggers are Section 2 non-renewal/notice and the Section 1 delivery-failure right), so we are not in walk-away territory, but the clause fails every fallback element (successor assignment, notice, consent for other assignments, reasonableness standard). We have therefore taken the fallback rather than the asymmetric preferred position: one short mutual provision permitting successor assignment on written notice and requiring not-unreasonably-withheld consent for any other assignment, leaving Section 10.3 otherwise untouched.

mappings.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
A successor assignment requires written notice.
Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add mutual successor-assignment right with notice and a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard for other assignments
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10.3 only confirms the Agreement binds successors and assigns; it does not govern assignment, so HDI could transfer this Agreement (including to a competitor) without our consent. We have added our fallback position: either Party may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets on written notice, and any other assignment requires the other Party's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

ops.text: Either Party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice to the other Party. Any other assignment of this Agreement requires the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.
